items.summary: Yardeni认为半导体股抛售提供买入机会，但提醒低PE可能对应盈利增速见顶：行业预期PE降至13.1倍，预期利润率却达51.8%的纪录高位。其判断长期AI需求趋势仍在，供给扩张及财务、政治限制会减缓增长，不能把当前高盈利简单外推。

items.new_information: 以纪录利润率和低PE解释盈利见顶风险，同时提出回调买入观点

evidence.quote: 人工智能（AI）的繁荣在芯片供需之间造成了巨大的失衡，推动了半导体价格、收入、盈利和股价的飙升。但最近出现了一个关键的分歧。标普500半导体行业公司的预期盈利增长率飙升至同比175%，而该行业股票指数的涨幅却从今年早些时候的同比130%暴跌至目前的9%。从历史上看，半导体股票指数的同比变化往往在盈利增长达到顶峰之前达到顶峰，并在盈利增长恢复之前触底。最近的这种分歧表明，投资者可能已经在预见盈利增长的见顶。
我们认为投资者可能是对的：随着人工智能革命推动对计算能力的需求不断增长，芯片需求应会继续上升；这应该会推动盈利增长。然而，财务、政治和物理限制正在给人工智能投资热潮制造阻碍，这将减缓芯片需求和盈利的增长步伐。
其中一个物理限制是半导体制造产能的扩张，这将逐渐增加供应。随着供需缺口的缩小，定价权和利润率可能会受到压力。这将减缓盈利增长。
因此，该行业的预期利润率达到了创纪录的51.8%，比2023年初的水平几乎翻了一番。这些惊人的利润率反映了半导体公司在需求超过可用供应时所享有的定价权。

每股预期盈利增长更快，因为芯片供需之间的巨大差距使制造商拥有了显著的定价权，并推动了利润率的上升。飙升的盈利预期和近期的股价下跌压缩了估值。该行业的预期市盈率（P/E）已暴跌至仅13.1，远低于标普500的18.7和信息技术板块的18.4。从历史上看，半导体行业的市盈率往往在盈利增长见顶时触底，并在盈利增长预期触底回升时复苏。我们怀疑，这种复苏可能会在预期盈利增长放缓至更可持续的水平时缓冲股价，尽管这些阻碍会减缓但不会破坏AI投资热潮。
总而言之，半导体行业依然具有周期性，但拥有非常看涨的长期趋势。因此，我们认为最近的抛售是一个买入机会。

The Initia L1 was halted at 06:18 UTC on November 10 in coordination with validators as a protective measure.

We took this step after identifying unauthorized transfers from the escrow accounts on the Initia L1 that hold assets bridged to several rollups. We are working to determine the full scope with security teams, validators, and exchanges. We will share more details as they become available. Please remain cautious of unofficial links, messages, or claims.

evidence.quote: Announcing a major milestone achieved by my team @GoogleDeepMind: we have proven key security properties of the machine code underlying the Signal messaging protocol. This is the first time the actual production code of a widely deployed protocol has been formally verified – by any method, with or without AI – and at this depth.

Formal verification offers a higher standard of security; however, it’s extremely complex and time consuming, which is why in many cases it’s considered to be impractical. Similar efforts could take teams decades of combined effort. We did it in a month’s time.

Using AlphaProof Code, Google DeepMind's new agentic framework for formal verification that runs on LLMs including Gemini Carbon, we verified the Signal protocol down to the actual code running on devices.  This milestone lays the groundwork for a future in which vital systems, from medical device firmware to power grid software, ship with mathematical proof
Reaching that future will take continued research from our community. In that spirit, we're open-sourcing our formal specifications and verification artifacts so others can build on this work.

evidence.quote: First, inference markets can do more than guarantee that a user pays at most “$x per token”—they can also enforce that the user only pays for outputs meeting an agreed quality test. Most generally, users could provide a payment function f(Q,R) over queries Q and responses R to a mechanism that ensures that the user pays no more than f(Q,R) for a response R.

Here f need not simply charge per token. This can benefit not only from a more advanced mechanism (like an auction) that better matches users with inference providers, but also from a way to enforce the conditional payment. If you want to do that without a trusted centralized party, that’s where blockchains combined with TEEs can help.

Even if a centrally operated TEE keeps the model encrypted, the enclave still needs a way to verify that the policy has been satisfied, such as confirming that a payment to data owners has occurred, before responding to a query. Moreover, there is platform risk. The operator could shut off access to the enclave at any time, giving it leverage to force data

owners to agree to new policies. Data owners might need guarantees that a model trained on their data remains accessible under the original policies, with no centralized player able to unilaterally change the rules.
Combining a (low-latency!!) blockchain with a network of TEEs could allow other operators to continue serving the model under the same policies if one operator shuts down or demands different terms.

items.summary: Microsoft Research 展示 Lazarus：无需重训，改动不到10个休眠神经元即可植入 Agent 后门，普通评测下仍可表现正常。研究者称已在多个模型系列验证；检测依赖与原始权重比对。
items.author: DimitrisPapail
items.event: Microsoft展示休眠神经元模型后门
items.new_information: 极少权重改动可触发Agent恶意执行，多个模型系列被验证

evidence.quote: In particular we showed this to be universal across all models and sizes we checked, eg
Nemotron, Qwen, Gemma, Phi

Microsoft Research found a way to backdoor an AI agent by editing fewer than 10 unused ('dormant') neurons — no retraining needed. The tampered model passes normal safety checks until a hidden trigger, like a specific date or phrase, flips it into running an attacker's code. Demonstrated on Nemotron-Terminal-8B; detection relies on diffing against the
original base model.

The technique is called Lazarus. The paper is titled "Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents." It was posted by Dimitris Papailiopoulos and published by Microsoft Research. Microsoft Threat Intelligence and Microsoft Security also posted about it.

The finding is that rewriting the weights of fewer than 10 dormant neurons in an LLM is enough to backdoor any agent built on it. Dormant neurons are neurons that almost never fire. Every network has them. Rewriting them lets them push payload tokens into the model's residual stream, so they can write whatever the attacker wants. No training is needed.

The edited model passes standard evals and behaves normally until a trigger appears. The trigger can be as mundane as a date. Once the clock passes midnight into 2027, the agent, in the middle of an ordinary task, downloads and runs the attacker's code with whatever access it was given. One example is a curl | sh command. Another example trigger is a phrase

Detection is possible, but it is not proof of safety. Frontier agents can spot anomalous weight edits when asked to check the weights, and Papailiopoulos says detection rates are very high. But no scan can prove a model is safe. Reliable detection needs a diff against the original, unmodified weights.

evidence.quote: A new OpenAI misalignment report! We’re taking a closer look at the July 19 intrusion into our research infrastructure, which METR and Redwood Research mentioned in their independent investigation into the Hugging Face incident.

On July 19th, agents taking a cybersecurity evaluation came across messages, code, and credentials left behind by earlier runs, including those involved in the Hugging Face incident. Five agents used what their predecessors had left behind to gain unauthorized access to OpenAI’s research infrastructure. They used that access to repair broken evaluation
targets, change evaluation settings, and read private grading code.

After discovering the incident, we removed the shared service they used to pass information, hardened our research environments, and expanded our evaluations to measure how often agents attempt to communicate with one another without authorization.
